solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

indicators.note: something gone astray has wandered from its proper place, so the following letters are out of order

blocks.note: twelve letters taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A castaway who wandered off course now lies marooned somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the letters of 'lies stranded' rearrange to the answer, and the full sentence describes where a castaway ends up.
explanation.definitionFit: A remote uninhabited isle is exactly where a shipwrecked person who went off course would be left marooned.

blocks.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely
an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: An instruction to obey what your mother taught you.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogma is a body of doctrine laid down by an authority, the set principles a church or school instils.

indicators.note: to protect something is to wrap around it, so one piece encloses the other
extremists are those at the ends, so only the outer letters of the word before are kept

blocks.note: the back is the spine
the first and last letters of disloyal

explanation.surface: Rod is the name of a backstabber shielding traitors on the fringes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rod's back' reads as a man returning; Rod is in fact the definition and 'back' is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A spindle is a slender rod or pin on which thread is wound or something rotates.

clue.text: Stir-crazy riverside dweller comes up for coffee

indicators.note: crazy suggests something jumbled and out of its right order
in a down clue, coming up means reading from bottom to top, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
an otter lives on riverbanks

explanation.surface: An otter going stir-crazy surfaces in search of an espresso.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stir-crazy' looks like one hyphenated phrase, but 'Stir' is the fodder and 'crazy' the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ristretto is a very short, concentrated shot of espresso coffee made with less water.

clue.text: County where most laugh when playing instrument

indicators.note: playing implies messing about with the words before, putting them in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a keyboard instrument

explanation.surface: A place where audiences laugh hardest whenever a musician performs.
explanation.walkthrough: South Glamorgan was a Welsh county, containing Cardiff, from 1974 to 1996.
explanation.definitionFit: It was an administrative county of south Wales, abolished in the 1996 reorganisation of local government.

blocks.note: taken as written
R is Romeo in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a rival is a competitor or contender

explanation.surface: A suitor turns up hot on Romeo's heels to make an entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: Read it as A, then a contender coming after Romeo: the single letter for Romeo sits between A and the rival.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrival is the act of coming in or reaching a place, so it serves as a noun for an entrance.

clue.text: Love affair and marriage after initiation of divorce

indicators.note: an initiation is a beginning, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: first letter of divorce
a marriage is an alliance between two families

explanation.surface: A tale of a fling followed by a wedding once the divorce proceedings start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the marriage word behind the single letter; 'and' simply joins definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A dalliance is a casual romantic or sexual relationship, a light flirtation not meant seriously.

indicators.note: over as in knocked over: the letters are upset and fall into a new order

blocks.note: an Aga is a brand of kitchen range cooker
taken as written without the apostrophe, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A distance measure apparently not beyond twenty units.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cross-reference: 20 across is ANTI. An Aga is a heavy cast-iron British cooker, so 'Range' is the brand, not a distance.
explanation.definitionFit: ANTI means opposed to, and against is its everyday synonym as a preposition of opposition.

clue.text: During danger, they say you were ultimately silly

indicators.note: what people say is heard rather than seen, so the next word is taken for its sound
something happening during a thing sits inside it
ultimately means at the very end, so only the last letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: peril is danger
the letter U sounds like you
last letter of were

explanation.surface: Someone's foolish behaviour when faced with a threat is being gossiped about.
explanation.walkthrough: The sound-alike U goes inside PERIL just after its first letter, then the E is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Puerile means childishly foolish or trivial, describing silly, immature behaviour.

blocks.note: surface reading: a hint for a crossword solver named Kate
setter's reading: the woman's name, given a new form, turns into a common verb meaning seize

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a hint to help a friend called Kate.
explanation.walkthrough: Change the shape of the four letters of Kate and you get the first word of the answer, so the phrase literally describes what happens to Kate.
explanation.definitionFit: When a plan takes shape it gradually forms and becomes clearer, which is to develop.

blocks.note: having less hair is being balder
a dash is a short sprint race

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea of a contest for those losing their hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Balderdash is senseless talk or writing, an old-fashioned word for rubbish or tosh.

indicators.note: when something leaves, it departs, so it is taken out of the word

blocks.note: to duck a question is to dodge it
taken as written

explanation.surface: A duck waddling away from a household cleaning machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' looks like the bird or a cricket score of nothing; here it is the verb meaning dodge.
explanation.definitionFit: A void is an empty space, as a vacuum is space containing nothing at all.

indicators.note: some means only part, so the answer is a run of letters inside the words that follow

blocks.note: inside the end of people and the start of attempt

explanation.surface: A few folk try to come together.
explanation.definitionFit: In dressmaking a gather and a pleat are both folds drawn into fabric to shape it.

blocks.note: plain means simple, unadorned
a tiff is a minor quarrel or misunderstanding

explanation.surface: A man grumbling over a straightforward mix-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaintiff is the party who brings a complaint against another in a court of law.

clue.text: Encourage growth of aubergine down under

blocks.note: to egg on is to encourage
a plant is something that grows

explanation.surface: Advice to nurture an aubergine crop in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down under' is not a placement signal but means Australia, where aubergine is called by this name, as in America.
explanation.definitionFit: The aubergine's name in Australian and American English is a regional synonym for the same vegetable.

clue.text: Wicked anti-immigration old Tory party leader

blocks.note: wicked means bad
Enoch Powell, Conservative politician remembered for his 1968 speech against immigration

explanation.surface: A harsh judgement on a former Conservative chief hostile to immigrants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tory party leader' reads as one phrase, but the old Tory belongs to the wordplay and only 'party leader' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Kemi Badenoch became leader of the British Conservative Party in 2024.

clue.text: Perhaps Sheikh Al Maktoum could give us airtime

indicators.note: could give us suggests the following letters might be made into something else by reworking them

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A Gulf ruler might grant us broadcast slots.
explanation.walkthrough: The Al Maktoum family rules Dubai; 'Perhaps' marks a sheikh of that family as one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheikhs of the Al Maktoum dynasty are citizens of the UAE, so each is an example of a person from the Emirates.

indicators.note: reading something out means voicing it, so the answer is what the words sound like

blocks.note: the author speaking of themselves says I will, contracted

explanation.surface: A writer plans to give a public reading of an extract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passage' looks like an extract from a book, which fits the author; it is in fact a walkway.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a walkway between rows of seats, a passage in a church, theatre or shop.

indicators.note: in a down clue a supporter holds things up from below, so the piece before this word is placed after the piece following it

blocks.note: graffiti is street art, abbreviated to ST and ART
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Is the French really behind that spray-painted wall art?
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'supporting' puts the French article below, at the end. The question mark flags graffiti read as 'street art', with ST the usual abbreviation for street.
explanation.definitionFit: To startle is to give someone a sudden shock or fright, a verb meaning to take aback.

indicators.note: to here means belonging to, so the answer is found as part of the next word

blocks.note: letters three to six of infantilisation

explanation.surface: Someone objects to treating adults like children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opposed to' reads as one phrase, and arguably it is the whole definition with the hidden signal left implicit.
explanation.definitionFit: Anti as an adjective means against or hostile to something.

clue.text: Hummus and baba ghanoush placed before Arab with a drink problem

blocks.note: both are dips eaten with bread
someone from Oman is an Arab
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mezze platter set before an Arab man who drinks too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'placed before' simply sets the order of the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Dipsomania is an old clinical term for alcoholism, an uncontrollable craving for alcohol.

clue.text: Do this with sorrows or learn to swim instead

blocks.note: first meaning: the idiom for blotting out grief with alcohol
second meaning: what happens in deep water to someone who cannot swim, as in 'sink or swim'

explanation.surface: Advice to someone grieving: drink the pain away, or take swimming lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: Each half is a cryptic pointer to the same verb: one through the drinker's idiom, the other through the alternative to swimming.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to die under water, and in the idiom about sorrows it means to blot them out with drink.

clue.text: I call back, after a change of heart and… it's a long story

indicators.note: going back means travelling the opposite way, so the word is read backwards
the heart is the middle, and changing it means the central letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
to dial is to call on the phone

explanation.surface: Someone who rang back after rethinking things warns it is a lengthy tale.
explanation.walkthrough: I plus the turned-round phone word gives five letters; the middle three are then rearranged, a 'change of heart'.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's Iliad is a very long epic poem telling the story of the Trojan War.

clue.text: Rider said to select an entrance

indicators.note: said means spoken aloud, so the answer sounds like the words that follow

blocks.note: to select is to pick, and an entrance is a door

explanation.surface: A horseman is told to choose which way in to take.
explanation.definitionFit: A picador is the mounted bullfighter who goads the bull with a lance from horseback.

clue.text: Got into ripe bananas as selfish behaviour

indicators.note: going into something means being placed inside it
bananas means crazy, so the letters go wild and rearrange

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone greedily helped themselves to the soft fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' looks like the fruit that is ripe; it is the signal to rearrange. GOT then sits after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An ego trip is an activity done mainly to boost one's own self-importance.

clue.text: Dined in style, housed by unrestrained timely help

indicators.note: to style something is to give it a new fashion, so the letters are reshaped
something housed by another lives inside it

blocks.note: freed means let loose
the seven letters of the two words, rearranged

explanation.surface: A lavish meal paid for by a generous, free-spending benefactor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dined in style' reads as one phrase, but 'Dined in' is the fodder; the rearranged letters sit after the first two of FREED.
explanation.definitionFit: From the proverb 'a friend in need is a friend indeed': someone who helps when you most need it.
